articleTitle: The Optimal Returns IntegratiOnal Network - ORION
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: The Optimal Returns IntegratiOnal Network - ORION is produced innovatively to elaborate significant parameters of the portfolio optimization domain, such as: i) trends on investors patterns, ii) the Entropic effect on investors in the Chaotic effects of the Markets in SDEs by Tsallis Statistics and Fractal Market Hypothesis-FMH, iii) the detection of the optimal classifier on 60 Modular models of plain Nets of Neurals and Hybrid Neuro-Genetics to support the optimal investment policy, are examined.

articleTitle: The Dehumidification Process and its Influence on the Insulation System Quality Index
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: Power transformers, during their operation, are subjected to various stresses that cause a certain aging of their insulation system. Through this paper we aim to highlight the importance of revitalization/treatment/regeneration processes, which aim to improve the physico-chemical parameters of the insulation system, but also to extend the lifetime of power transformers in operation. The paper presents two case studies, which emphasize the importance of the application of drying processes to the transformer insulation system. The obtained results encourage the application of methods of revitalization of the insulation system by oil regeneration (improvement of the quality index), drying and purification of solid insulation.

articleTitle: A Procedure with MySQL Python for Developing Data Warehouse and Analytics Using Data from a Greek Soft Drinks Company
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: The research focuses on the process of creating a data warehouse to meet the decision-making needs of a Greek beverage company. The data cover the period from 2018 to 2022. The developed data warehouse schema follows the star schema, with one fact table and five-dimension tables. Based on this structure, a web application was developed in PHP, which displays reports, charts, and analyses on the company's performance through interactive queries. Additionally, prediction functions tailored to the company's data were developed in Python. The process followed, the queries for creating the data warehouse, as well as the commands for creating analyses and predictions, serve as a useful guide for other companies that wish to upgrade the capabilities of their ERP systems.

articleTitle: MD Simulation Study of Complex Formation Between LysHisArg Dendrimer and Molecules of AlaGluAspGly Bioactive Peptide
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: In previous papers we studied behavior of lysine dendrimers of second generation with charged double lysine and arginine (KK, RR) spacers, hydrophobic double leucine, alanine and glycine (LL, AA, GG) spacers and pH dependent double histidine (HH) dipeptide spacers inserted between each pair of neighboring branching points of dendrimer. We also studied their complexes of these dendrimers with molecules of several bioactive peptides (including AEDG tetrapeptide) necessary for delivery of these peptides to different cells. It was shown that lysine dendrimers with charged internal insertions are good for delivery of oppositely charged oligopeptides and genetic material while dendrimers with hydrophobic internal insertions are good for delivery of bioactive hydrophobic molecules. In present work we study the complexes of molecules of AEDG peptide and dendrimer with repeating unit LysHisArg containing histidine-arginine (HisArg, HR) spacer. In our case aminoacid residues (H and R) in spacers of dendrimer are different and the charge of H residue depends on pH. We performed molecular dynamics simulations of the complexation of 16 AEDG molecules with a dendrimer at two different value of pH: a) pH>7 with fully uncharged histidines (H) and b) pH<5 with fully protonated (Hp) histidines in aqueous solution with explicit counterions. It was found that the dendrimer with protonated histidines could carry a larger number of AEDG tetrapeptide molecules.

articleTitle: ML-based Fault Tree Analysis of Industrial Router Reliability in the System IIoT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: For today's complex and expensive systems, such as an industrial router in an Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) network, it is important to ensure high operational reliability. The router is a complex system consisting of many subsystems, and an important task is to identify possible failures and faults of its subsystems in order to prevent them in time, or to parry and eliminate them. One of the methods of system reliability assessment is the method of cutting, which includes fault tree analysis (FTA). FTA allows, using the obtained and analysed statistical data, to build a fault tree with a given level of detail, and to determine the probabilities of failures of one or another subsystem. In this paper a detailed tree of failures and failures of hardware (HW), software (SW), and hardware-software (HW-SW) of the industrial router of the IIoT system is developed. The tree is built with the use of program code, using ensemble supervised ML algorithms in Python. The obtained graphical dependencies and obtained probabilities of failures of router's subsystems as a part of quantitative analysis, allowed us to determine for the given initial data the most exposed to the risk of failure of the subsystem of the industrial router in the system IIoT.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Vibrations of the “Rotor-Weak Conductive Fluid-Foundation” System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: A new generalized dynamic model of the rotor system has been developed, which considers the interconnected oscillations within the “rotor - weakly conductive fluid - foundation” system. This model incorporates various factors, including linear eccentricity, movements of the fluid and rotor, frictional forces, base vibrations, rolling bearings and their nonlinear properties, and the magnetic field's influence on the fluid. The motion equations for this system were formulated and solved analytically. The analysis of the system's oscillations revealed key features of its dynamics. The frequencies and amplitudes, which significantly influence the system's dynamic behavior, were investigated, and determined.

articleTitle: Security of Clusters: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: Security of computer networks and clusters is crucial for ensuring connectivity to the outside world and cloud services to not be interrupted. To prevent unauthorized access to them we must ensure that we have robust encryption and authentication of the connection between the servers and clients. To ensure security standards, security audits and updates are crucial to prevent threats in cluster environments. Firewall, intrusion detection and prevention systems are great assets for strengthening clusters security. This article gives an overview of security of clusters.

articleTitle: Object Oriented Cellular Automaton for Multiple Lane Road Traffic Noise Mapping
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: Due to the traffic and its noise emission, road infrastructures represent a major source of illness. Noise measurement campaigns in order to produce map noises are essential for the decision-making of urban and suburban areas, yet wide measurements turn out to be expensive and unpractical. In this manner, simulation tools to help predict noise emitted from road traffic are designed. In this paper, a cellular automaton simulates traffic of a multiple-lane road, and the associated noise map of the road are calculated. The cellular automaton relies on the stochastic Nagel-Schreckenberg method. The real-world quantities are then assigned to the cellular automaton, giving each vehicle a speed in km/h. Using the common model of noise assessment CNOSSOS-EU, noise power levels are assigned to vehicles according to their kinematic parameters. The spreading of noise through the map is done through point-like source propagation respecting the time of propagation. The results highlight the effect of the number of lanes and traffic frequency on the noise maps.

articleTitle: A Procedure for Optimization of Placement Products in Large Industrial Areas of a Greek Soft Drinks Company
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: In this paper we present the process of optimal placement of industrial products (pallets) in mapped ware-houses and specifically in a soft drink company in Greece. The optimization criterion is to minimize the cost of moving the lifting machine that places the products in specific positions. The computational method of optimal placement of industrial products receives data from the automatic product count of the mapped warehouse and from the sales predictive model. Therefore, the computational method, having knowledge of the location and number of products in the warehouse and the prediction of sales for each product, places the products produced in an optimal way. Automatic product counting is carried out using an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) which developed and applied in soft drink company in Greece. The sales prediction is carried out through a prediction model which developed in a soft drink company in Greece.

articleTitle: Using Escape Rooms to Support Learners’ “Equations-Escapes” in e-learning: Applied MCIEC Model in Mathematics Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: In the contemporary digital age, particularly in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic, educators are faced with the need to adapt and integrate new pedagogical approaches and technologies into the realm of education. Within the domain of mathematics, longstanding challenges in comprehending the subject have been widely recognized. In response to this issue, an electronic course entitled “Equations-Escapes from the Museum of Mathematics” has been developed to enhance sixth-grade mathematics instruction. This course employs digital escape rooms and is delivered entirely online through the Moodle platform, following the MCIEC model. Its primary objective is to augment mathematical proficiency, cultivate student motivation, and nurture 21st-century competencies. The efficacy of the course was appraised through a pilot study involving 50 educators, and subsequent statistical analysis of the collected data substantiated the validation of all alternative hypotheses devised in accordance with the research inquiries. Consequently, this educational intervention is deemed successful in achieving the stated objectives.

articleTitle: Combining Autoencoder and Cellular Neural Networks for Enhanced Direct Multi-Step Forecasting of Short and Long-Term Multivariate Time Series in Battery Health Monitoring: A Preliminary Feasibility Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: The paper proposes a conceptual framework for battery health monitoring by combining Autoencoders and Cellular Neural Networks (CeNNs) to enhance direct multi-step forecasting of short- and long-term battery health parameters, such as State of Charge (SoC) and Remaining Useful Life (RUL). The primary innovation is using Autoencoders for dimensionality reduction and noise filtering from multivariate time series data, followed by CeNNs to model spatial dependencies between battery cells and their temporal evolution. The Autoencoder compresses high-dimensional battery data into a latent space, from which CeNNs forecast future health states. This hybrid architecture enables accurate predictions without the recursive steps of traditional models, thus avoiding error compounding. While this paper outlines the theoretical and pipeline design, future work will focus on model implementation, performance evaluation using real-world data, and optimizing it for real-time predictive maintenance applications. The conceptual framework presents a novel approach to addressing the complex spatio-temporal dynamics in battery systems, offering a scalable solution for various battery types.

articleTitle: Determination of BTEX at a Site Near an Oil Refinery in Minatitlán, Veracruz, México
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: Human emissions can disrupt natural cycles and contribute to air pollution. This study focuses on analyzing volatile organic compounds known as BTEX (benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, and xylene isomers) emitted mainly by oil and gas extraction as well as consumer products. The study was conducted near the Lazaro Cárdenas del Río refinery in Minatitlan, Veracruz, to measure BTEX concentrations. A risk analysis indicated a significant cancer risk (LTCR) for the population, particularly in children, surpassing the limits set by the US EPA and WHO. While the non-cancer risk (HQ) is within limits, the overall risk index (HI) underscores the necessity for mitigation measures to safeguard public health.

articleTitle: Tests Towards Building a Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) Link
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: We report on preliminary steps performed toward implementing a Free Space Optical (FSO) Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) link between our institute (INFLPR) and the Natl. Inst. for Phys. Nucl. Eng. (NIPNE). Besides some of the technical aspects that we address, we also use open-source software development kits (SDK) such as Qiskit to test different QKD protocols and transfer functions.

Author Keywords: Free Space Optical (FSO) Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) link

articleTitle: MeDAl – The Creation of Medical Dissertations Corpus in Albanian for Medical NLP
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: Natural Language Processing (NLP) has been widely used to surface the intelligence embedded in textual documents that could not be leveraged through traditional data mining techniques. While NLP models can be shifted with almost no change across domains and languages, training materials such as corpora cannot. Currently, there are no available domain-specific corpora for the training of medical NLP models in the Albanian language. Therefore, in this paper, we introduce the creation of the Medical Dissertations Corpus in Albanian (MeDA1), a 6M words corpus in Albanian in the medical domain. The corpus was built from parsing and cleaning more than 300 dissertations published in the last 10 years by the University of Medicine in Tirana. The corpus can be used in the training or continuous training of NLP models used in medical settings - we intend to use the corpus in a Named Entity Recognition (NER) task for Electronic Health Records (EHR) in the Albanian language. In this paper, we describe in detail the process of PDF parsing and text cleaning that we have conducted for the creation of MeDAl.

articleTitle: On Cyber Vulnerability of MASS: A Simulation Experiment to Counter a Rudder Controller Attack
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is twofold: (1) to underscore the vulnerability of Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASSs) to cyber-attacks and (2) to emulate, using a concrete example, a cyber-attack on a rudder controller and its neutralization using a Kalman filter and a PID regulator. Accordingly, the first part of the paper will be based on a scoping review of relevant articles in the domain, including some MASSs projects, probabilistic modelling techniques to address MASSs' vulnerabilities, and cyber-security analysis. The second part of the work will deal with the simulation of a cyber-attack on the rudder controller testbed and its elimination. It is believed that the cyber-attack could occur through an unauthorized intrusion into the MASS Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system and PLC (Programmable Logic Controller) ladder logic code. The MATLAB/Simulink will be used for the experiment on the testbed. By optimization of the system parameters, the malicious interference caused by the arbitrary shaped periodic signal malicious intrusion into the control system will be eliminated. This will provide the optimal control of the analyzed MASS rudder controller, and a foundation for creating cyber-attacks prevention training data sets.

articleTitle: Hybrid Co-Simulation Framework for Cyber-Physical Systems-Based Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: Developing safety-critical cyber-physical systems (CPS) relies heavily on human interaction and cognitive assessment. The possibility to evaluate with real-time data certain scenarios between the CPS and its components brings benefits in increasing the performance of the systems. Thus, this paper proposes the concept of co-simulation in which physical systems and communication systems can be modeled simultaneously, starting from two possible applications usually encountered (energy and medicine). The co-simulation method started from the real case study of a microgrid, where the data from the hardware components were sent both to a located application and an application over 250 km away, in this way simulating possible security breaches, data accuracy, and transmission errors. A later simulation framework was created for the case study in medicine that will be analyzed based on the work methodology created, but maintaining the particularities of critical applications in medicine and the necessity of customizing scenarios and contextual analyses for a pharyngoesophageal prosthesis.

articleTitle: Using Interpretive Structural Modeling for the Implementation of the Balanced Scorecard to Support Evaluation and Decision-Making in the Performance Management of Telecommunications Services of a Public Operator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: This article aims to explore and improve the strategic management methods used for the balanced scorecard of a public telecommunications infrastructure operator. First, an inventory of traditional qualitative methods, such as the Causal loop diagram (CLD) and others, will be conducted to assess their weaknesses and limitations. For this purpose, comprehensive criteria for a critical evaluation will be formulated and justified. Then, a succinct and comprehensive presentation of the Interpretive structural modeling (ISM) methodology will be provided, with a particular focus on the final steps that support strategic decision-making. The ISM methodology will then be applied to strategically manage the public operator's balanced scorecard, enabling the analysis of complex interactions between the factors influencing this management. Strategic decisions will be facilitated through the use of the ISM model. Finally, a comparison will be made between the use of CLD and traditional ISM in this context to demonstrate the superiority of ISM over CLD in assisting the strategic management of such an infrastructure.

Author Keywords: Interpretive structural modeling and Causal loop diagram

articleTitle: Nonparametric Estimation of the Conditional Bivariate Distribution Function of Censored Gap Times
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: A major goal in recurrent events analysis is to estimate the bivariate distribution function. This estimation is crucial across various fields and applications, as it helps clarify the patterns of recurring events and their underlying patterns. ‘Gap time’ refers to the duration between consecutive occurrences of an event, while the bivariate distribution function represents the joint probability distribution of two such gap times. Despite significant advancements in this area, most existing methods assume independent censoring and neglect the impact of covariates. Therefore, the primary aim of this paper is to develop and introduce nonparametric estimation methods for the bivariate distribution function that incorporate covariate measures. This study seeks to provide more precise and applicable tools for analyzing recurrent event data, thereby enhancing the understanding and interpretation of such events in practical scenarios.

articleTitle: Self-Consumption Configurations for Renewable Energy Sharing in Condominiums (CACERs)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: The growing trend of on-site energy production, particularly through photovoltaic (PV) systems in apartment buildings and condominiums, presents a significant challenge: efficiently distributing the generated electricity amongst individual units. This study explores Self-Consumption Configurations for Renewable Energy Sharing in Condominiums (CACERs) as a solution to this hurdle and introduces a proposal model of power sharing as alternative model. This shift towards decentralized energy production aligns with the growing emphasis on empowering passive consumers. Recent European Directives highlight the importance of active end-user participation in the energy system, which includes residential, commercial, and tertiary buildings - substantial contributors to overall energy consumption. These “end-users” can become active participants either directly or through collaborative aggregations. To address the challenge of energy distribution within condominiums utilizing CACERs, this paper provides a comprehensive overview of the current state of CACERs in Italy. A case study of a typical urban condominium serves as the reference for this analysis. The study explores energy and economic assessments for the condominium, focusing on both the CACER and Power Sharing models. This analysis will provide valuable insights into the feasibility and benefits of these CACERs for condominiums in Italy.

articleTitle: A Stacking Ensemble Technique for Mechanical Fault Detection in Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: The effective and accurate detection of faults in inductive electric motors is crucial to ensure their reliability and minimize costly downtime. In this study, after discussing various faults, including imbalance faults, that can arise in inductive motors for various industrial applications, we have presented a stacking ensemble learning technique for fault detection. In this technique, SVM, ELM, and MLP were considered as base learners while logistic regression was used as the meta-model. The results of the experiment have underscored the importance and effectiveness of using Machine Learning, particularly the stacking ensemble learning technique, to improve the accuracy of fault detection in inductive motors. Future work exploring and comparing other ensemble learning techniques to the presented stacking technique, and autoencoders can offer an exciting avenue to consider.

articleTitle: Optimization of Double Wishbone Suspension: Evaluating the Performance of Classes of Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: Double wishbone suspension systems are employed in high-performance vehicles owing to their superior control over wheel motion. The design of a double-wishbone suspension is a challenging multi-objective problem due to the many inter- related quantities that are key in determining its performance and vary during its motion. The design activity is thus a time-consuming and complex iterative process that aims to tune their variation and minimize deviations from the desired performance characteristics while requiring the satisfaction of mechanical constraints. Computational optimization methods can be integrated into the design activity only after an assessment of their capability to support efficiently and effectively an iterative workflow. In this work, we start with the mathematical modeling of the camber angle of the double wishbone suspension. Then, we use the multi-model optimization approach that includes metaheuristic algorithms (Genetic Algorithms, Particle Swarm Optimization, Gradient Descent, and Ant Colony Optimization) and classical methods (Nelder-Mead, Interior Point, Simulated Annealing, and Random Search). These methods are assessed in terms of objective value, computational time, and memory usage in an effort to minimize the variation of camber angles from the specified constraints. The results prove that the Interior Point method is more accurate and efficient in optimizing the suspension's camber angle across its operational range, followed by other classical methods.

articleTitle: Use of Machine Learning for Implementation of a Hydrocarbon Well Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: Hydrocarbon exploration and production depend on a solid understanding of subsurface properties and recoverable volumes. Without this knowledge, the likelihood of low hydrocarbon recovery from reservoirs increases significantly. Given the substantial investments required, proceeding without a thorough understanding of the subsurface carries considerable risks. The main objective of this study is to create a well model using a machine learning-based approach to calculate reservoir permeability (related to a well's flow capacity) and predict hydrocarbon volumes based on expected rock, fluid, and geometry parameters for new wells. To achieve this, we analyzed four daily operational variables, including flowing bottom-hole pressure and well fluid production rates (oil, gas, and water), along with eight well variables that influence hydrocarbon recovery, collected from 11 wells. The methodology begins by creating a model to calculate the PVT properties of the well fluids. Next, a dataset is built, incorporating daily variables and calculated ones essential for modeling multiphase flow regimes observed in the well production histories, such as transient and boundary-dominated flows. These flow regime equations were then mathematically transformed into linear equations, leading to the development of four models for the multiphase flow regimes. This transformation enabled the application of supervised machine learning algorithms to build five linear regression models (SL, OLS, WLS, RLS, and BR) to estimate reservoir permeability (k) for each flow regime. Finally, a predictive model using the same five multiple linear regression methods was constructed to forecast recoverable hydrocarbon volumes based on eight key well variables. Most linear regression models demonstrated high coefficients of determination <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{R}^{2})$</tex> and favorable metrics, including MSE, RMSE, and MAE, indicating a high level of accuracy in estimating permeability, with consistent results expected in unconventional reservoirs. Furthermore, hydrocarbon volume predictions highlight the benefits of utilizing known geological, fluid, and well design parameters before drilling, enabling highly accurate forecasts of recoverable volumes.

articleTitle: Modal Decomposition Procedures for Non-Proportionally Damped Linear Systems in Structural Mechanics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: In this article a general method for modal decomposition of non-proportionally damped linear systems is considered. Firstly, a brief description of the classic modal analysis of the equations of motion of MDOFS with proportional damping, based on the real eigenvectors of the undamped system is given. Secondly, a brief literature review is presented about the numerical methods for decoupling the linear equations of motion based on quadratic eigenvalue problem. The author focuses especially on a method using a phase synchronization technique, which is similar to the here presented approach. The main part presents systematically variants of a general method for modal decomposition of damped MDOFS with symmetric damping matrix, incorporating non-proportional viscous damping. The main goal is to perform a real-space modal analysis of the equations of motion in state-space formulation. The assembly of a modal transformation matrix in real space is based on the conjugated complex right eigenvectors, or on a combination of the left and right complex eigenvectors of the system. The eigenvector normalization can be performed with respect to the general mass or to the general stiffness matrix. In all proposed variants the real-space modal transformation matrix is derived by a combination of two complex transformations. By the aid of computer algebra software analytical expressions are developed for this modal transformation basis, built with real and imaginary parts of the employed eigenvectors and the associated eigenvalues. All variants of the presented procedures include the case of proportional damping and retain the usual advantages of the classic modal decomposition. Based on the proposed general method, an analytical formula has been derived for the constant phase lag/lead in natural vibrations in the proportional damping case. As an exemplary numerical demonstration, one of the presented procedures is applied to the equations of motion of wind turbine rotor blade. The proposed method can be used in the modal analysis of structural systems, containing different damping and energy-loss mechanism, which can be described by non-proportional damping matrix.

Author Keywords: modal decomposition of the equations of motion
constant phase lag in natural vibrations

articleTitle: Model-Based Design and Analysis of an Adaptive Exoskeleton Glove for Remote Rehabilitation: Integrating Computer Vision and Flexor Actuation Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: Health services continually confront a range of challenges that are intricately tied to the geographical and economic conditions of each region, leading to the deterioration, or even absence, of medical care. E-Health offers a solution by enabling connections with healthcare providers for remote assistance through Information and Communication Technologies (ICTs), irrespective of the geographical constraints faced by individual patients. The current study proposes a four-stage methodology for designing a hand exoskeleton system aimed at patient rehabilitation. This methodology is substantiated through a practical case study, which demonstrates the development of a computer vision system, the assessment and engineering model called Twisted String Actuation System (TSAS), and the system's simulated integration within a virtual environment to validate the final design. The development of this methodology sets the stage for the introduction of novel remote rehabilitation tools, thereby providing individuals with limited resources or geographical barriers easier access to medical assistance.

articleTitle: Explainable AI for Biometrics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: Explainable AI has a cascading effect, causing increased transparency in decision-making processes, which fosters greater user trust and acceptance. This trust leads to wider adoption of AI technologies in sensitive applications like healthcare and finance, where understanding and accountability are essential. In this paper, we propose an explainable AI survey-based biometrics models. It consists first of a comprehensive review of current explainable AI techniques applied to biometrics, focusing on methods such as feature importance analysis, saliency maps, and rule-based models. We then assess these methods' effectiveness in enhancing transparency and interpretability within biometric systems. This paper proposes a comprehensive framework for integrating explainable AI techniques into biometric models to enhance transparency, trust, and usability. The framework leverages a combination of explainable AI techniques, including feature attribution methods, interpretable model architectures, and visualization tools, to enhance the transparency and accountability of biometric models.

articleTitle: Enhancing Downlink Throughput Prediction in 4G LTE Networks Using Ensemble Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: Forecasting downlink throughput in 4G LTE networks is essential for optimizing resource distribution, guaranteeing Quality of Service (QoS), and enhancing overall network efficacy. Conventional models, including statistical methods, frequently do not adequately represent the dynamic and nonlinear attributes of contemporary cellular networks. This paper examines the application of machine learning and ensemble learning methodologies to improve throughput prediction. We evaluate the efficacy of individual models, such as SVM, Decision Tree, MLP, and LSTM, alongside ensemble techniques, including Bagging, Boosting, and Stacking. Our experimental findings indicate that ensemble learning methods substantially surpass solitary models, with Bagging attaining the minimal RMSE. The enhanced efficacy of these methods is ascribed to their capacity to integrate multiple base learners, thereby mitigating overfitting and augmenting generalization in intricate network settings. The results indicate that ensemble learning methods provide a reliable means of improving throughput prediction in 4G LTE networks.

articleTitle: Enhancing Interpretive Structural Modeling (ISM) Through the Integration of Influence Signs: A Novel Approach for Advanced Systemic Assessment and Validation via an Illustrative Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: This paper examines the limitations of traditional Interpretive Structural Modeling (ISM), which is widely used to structure and prioritize interconnected elements in complex systems. Although ISM is effective, it inadequately accounts for the directional nature of influences (positive or negative) between variables. To address this gap, an extended version of the ISM methodology is proposed, incorporating influence signs into these relationships. This new approach enhances ISM's ability to capture the nuances of complex interactions, thereby improving support for strategic decision-making. The paper provides a detailed comparison of the traditional and new ISM methodologies, focusing on critical decision-making phases. A practical application is conducted on a nine-variable system describing population dynamics, demonstrating the improved efficacy of the new ISM method and offering a better understanding of the impact of influential relationships in complex systems.

articleTitle: Symmetric Fuzzy Stochastic Differential Equations of Itô Type: Uniqueness of Solution
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: In this paper we discuss stochastic differential equations in a special approach. Namely, the values of the mappings occurring there are fuzzy sets, and not single values of the real line, as usual. Moreover, the form of the equations under consideration is symmetric in the sense that terms of the drift and diffusion occur simultaneously on both sides of the equation and this is important for the properties of solutions. The main intention of the paper is to provide certain collections of conditions that must be met by the coefficients of the equation in order to claim that there is a unique solution to the considered symmetric fuzzy stochastic Itô-type differential equation. We present three such collections of conditions, each one weakening the conditions of the previous one. We also note that the obtained results can be applied to considerations of symmetric set-valued stochastic differential equations.

Author Keywords: modelling in fuzzy and stochastic environment

articleTitle: Hands in Motion: Developing a Real-Time Gesture Recognition System for Enhanced Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: This paper presents the development of an advanced system that has the ability to recognize hand gestures and also maps new ways for users to access the interfaces, using as main libraries OpenCV, but also a microframework powerful enough MediaPipe to transform sign language into text. The system involves obtaining both static and dynamic images through a real-time camera, from which key hand features such as wrists, joints and degrees of freedom are extracted and identified. The gestures are then categorized based on several labeled datasets and integrated into a friendly interface called Tkinter. Through the use and identification of gestures, users have the possibility to manipulate applications in a way that is free from the human-computer interaction. After some testing, it was concluded that the system is sufficiently robust and precise and also very capable of accommodating the conditions of various environments. This has a strong impact on the users of applications in the field of artificial intelligence, constituting a fundamentally necessary experience that covers and promotes human-computer interaction and social engagement by making it accessible also to members of deaf-mute communities. It is also a way of integrating them into today's society by providing new opportunities and last generation technologies.

articleTitle: Enhanced Time Series Forecasting: Integrating PatchTST with BERT Layers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Applied Mathematics & Computer Science (ICAMCS)
abstract: Time series forecasting is critical for various fields such as stock market prediction, weather forecasting, and risk management. Traditional models like ARIMA and SARIMA are limited in capturing non-linear and multivariate dependencies in time series data. Deep learning models such as LSTM and Transformer-based architectures have emerged to address these issues but come with challenges like overfitting and high computational complexity. This paper introduces PatchFusionBERT, a novel hybrid model that integrates BERT layers with PatchTST to overcome these limitations. PatchTST partitions long time series into smaller patches to capture local temporal patterns, while BERT layers enhance long-term dependency capture. Experimental results on the ETT dataset show that PatchFusionBERT significantly outperforms PatchTST in both short- and long-term horizons, especially in multivariate time series forecasting. PatchFusionBERT demonstrates improved forecasting accuracy while also being computationally efficient.
